title: Serverless: AWS Lambda, Cloudflare Workers, Vercel and Netlify

videos.script: A request arrives. Nobody on your team has a server waiting for it, and the page still loads. {{request}} That is serverless, and the name is misleading. There are servers. You just do not see them, patch them or choose how many there are. You hand over a function, and the provider runs it when something asks. {{function}} In this lesson you write one small handler in Python and call it on a laptop. That puts the contract between your code and the platform on the screen. Lambda is not involved in that part, and the lesson says so plainly. {{handler}} Then you look at what calls a function, and at why the first request after a quiet spell is slower than the rest. {{cold}} Then the bill. From the public price list you work out what three million requests a month cost. And you find the volume where a machine that is always on becomes the cheaper choice. {{bill}} Cloudflare Workers, Vercel and Netlify come next. They share the word serverless and not much else. The lesson ends with the limits, and with the kinds of work a function is the wrong answer for. {{limits}}
